decisions.question: Gate 1, hero concepts: which elf ranger (Forest resistance defender, player-elf) concept should go to TRELLIS?

decisions.decision: Approve hd-s42, then add a rear-view concept: 3 local Qwen candidates, about 55 GPU-min, projected in the cook (Recommended)
decisions.question: Gate 2, the unrigged 3D meshes: what should I do with the elf? (board 127.0.0.1:47841; measured limitations stated: invented near-black back on every seed, soft faces with smeared eye sockets, mitten hands, pointed ears only in texture, HD indistinguishable from default at 18-40 m)
conditions: A rear-view concept is generated locally (Qwen Image Edit Plus 2511 in WanGP, Scene mode), painted over an orthographic back render of hd-s42 with the approved front concept as identity reference; three candidates; the user selects one.
The selected rear view is projected onto back-visible texels only, occlusion-tested and blended at the sides; the front keeps the TRELLIS texture from the approved concept.
Cook repairs: remove specks, separate or curl the mitten hands, clean the face and skin, decimate to the 16k hero budget with baked normals and 1024 maps; consider small pointed ear geometry.

decisions.question: Gate 3 re-ship, delegated under the standing instruction of 2026-10-01: char-hero-elf with its maps of 1024 px or more halved (resize_maps.py, then meshopt_glb.mjs; geometry, skin and clips byte-identical) is in the running game (board _reviews/gate3-resize-large). The file falls from 1,046,544 to 745,264 bytes. In isolated renders 0.067% of its pixels differ by more than 8/255 at 18 m (0.525% at pixel ratio 1.75, 0.0% at 26 m), tone ratio 0.9983; in the game (three factions, 18 and 26 m, pixel ratio 1 and 1.75) at most 0.019% of a frame differs by more than 8/255. Close-ups are softer (13.395% of pixels over 8/255). Shader programs are unchanged. Should I ship it?

decidedBy.userMessage: Go ahead and since I approved all your recommended options before, go with your recommended options without asking for approval going forward.

supplementary.question: Gate 3 final approval: ship the three heroes tone-calibrated (recommended) or as cooked, together with the line soldier cook-016 Run fix, as shown in the running game?
supplementary.superseded: Re-shipped quantized: the exact same cook with KHR_mesh_quantization vertex data and rotation keys, about a third fewer bytes and visually identical in the game (_reviews/gate3-quantized-others).

supplementary.question: Gate 3 re-ship, delegated under the standing instruction of 2026-10-01: the line soldier, archer, captain, both bosses, the elf and guard heroes and the draft ox, re-encoded with KHR_mesh_quantization, are in the running game (board 127.0.0.1:47877, _reviews/gate3-quantized-others). They are 32% smaller (13,867,500 to 9,433,556 bytes); in the game at most 0.008% of a frame's pixels change by more than 8/255, and every clip frame passes the unchanged verifiers. The mountain sovereign stays float because quantization pushed two of its clips over the 2.0x strain limit. Should I ship the quantized models?

decidedBy.userMessage: Go ahead and since I approved all your recommended options before, go with your recommended options without asking for approval going forward.

supplementary.superseded: Re-shipped meshopt-compressed: the same cook with its vertices and triangles reordered for locality (the same vertex data and triangles, with the same winding) and EXT_meshopt_compression without lossy filters; about a fifth fewer bytes and unchanged in the game (_reviews/gate3-meshopt).

supplementary.question: Gate 3 re-ship, delegated under the standing instruction of 2026-10-01: all 23 shipped models, with their vertices and triangles reordered for locality and their geometry, skin and animation data compressed with EXT_meshopt_compression (no lossy filters), are in the running game (board 127.0.0.1:47896, _reviews/gate3-meshopt). Files fall 19.7% (23,330,396 to 18,733,460 bytes) and the gzip download GitHub Pages serves 6.9% (17,957,653 to 16,725,201 bytes), for 6,117 gzip bytes of decoder. Every model decodes to the same mesh, skin, clips and images; every frame-verifier metric is unchanged; of 213 game frames 200 are bit-identical and 13 differ in one pixel each; shader programs, draw calls (except +1-2 off-screen submissions in three shots), frame times and preload time show no measurable change. Should I ship the compressed models?

decidedBy.userMessage: Go ahead and since I approved all your recommended options before, go with your recommended options without asking for approval going forward.

supplementary.superseded: Re-shipped with its maps of 1024 px or more halved (resize_maps.py: a 2x2 box filter, as the GPU builds mip level 1, then meshopt_glb.mjs): the game camera never samples the cooked top level, so the frames are unchanged while the file shrinks by about a third and those maps' texture memory to a quarter (_reviews/gate3-resize-large).
